messages:
maria.g: quick q — we're mapping retention tiers for security logs. who decides which events go to long-term (7y) vs 90d? also need guidance on kms delegation for oncall pulls. do we have a safelist for siem exports so SRE can pull during incidents without full key unwrap? @alex.k @samir

alex.k: short — decision lives in the sec-retention-policy doc but it's not granular. we should add a tag->bucket mapping table. +1 for a timeboxed safelist for incident key-unwraps. current approach: CMK wrapping + proxy service for unwraps, not direct user decrypts.

samir: we already use a `forensics` tag in a few places that maps to long-term. rough proposal: `forensics` -> 7y, `auth` -> 1y, `telemetry` -> 90d. prod owners should opt-in to `forensics`. also prefer proxy pattern: only proxy has `kms:Decrypt`. users assume short-lived role to call proxy.

jess: heads up — compliance will want a written justification for any 7y retention. also require an auditable trail for all unwraps (who, why, TTL). add retention justification to tenant onboarding.

maria.g: ok can someone sketch the minimal iam/flow for timeboxed unwraps? ideally no permanent `kms:Decrypt` on user accounts.

alex.k: pseudo runbook sketch:

```
# KMS unwrap flow (sketch)
1. Oncall files incident ticket with ID and justification
2. Sec-oncall approves via Slack (emoji + link) -> approval recorded
3. Ops issues STS token to assume temp role `kms-unwrapper` (valid 1h)
4. Temp role calls proxy service endpoint
5. Proxy (service principal) performs KMS Decrypt with CMK and logs request to audit bucket
6. All unwraps stored under `audit/unwraps/<incident-id>.json`
```

samir: add: require OPA policy evaluation before STS issuance to check scope (which buckets, which IDs) and TTL. proxy should only return data blobs, not raw keys. also rotate CMK regularly and keep key version in audit.

devsecops-bot: PR gate: retention-buckets.tf modified in PR #1245 — security review requested from @security.

oncall: current manual process is slow during incidents. can we have an "urgent unwrap" path that still enforces human approval but uses an automated fast path? runbook needs a small checklist.

jess: automation ok but human approval required. ensure generated justification doc (approval, who, why) is automatically uploaded to `audit/unwraps/` and linked in ticket.

alex.k: also recommend adding safelist entries on the SIEM export side: give consumer apps expiring tokens scoped to read-only scrubbed exports instead of unwrapping keys. prefer tokenized export pipeline rather than granting unwrap perms.

maria.g: thanks everyone. action items: alex -> draft mapping table and runbook; samir -> propose KMS proxy role + OPA policy; jess -> compliance checklist + onboarding change; devsecops-bot -> block PR until review. i'll open a follow-up thread with the draft mapping. :thumbsup:
